Thought: Let me analyze the possible reactions between aldehydes and azo/diazo compounds:

1. Aldehydes (R-CHO) have a carbonyl group that is quite reactive.
2. Azo compounds (R-N=N-R) and diazo compounds (R-CH=N=N) contain nitrogen-nitrogen bonds.

When aldehydes react with azo or diazo compounds:
- Diazo compounds can react with aldehydes in the presence of catalysts to form various products
- One common reaction is the formation of polymers (polymerization)
- Azo compounds can initiate radical reactions with aldehydes
- These reactions often lead to chain reactions resulting in polymers

Looking at the options:
A. Formation of toxic gases - While some reactions might produce gases, this is not a characteristic effect
B. Isomerization to ketones - This is not a typical outcome
C. Polymerization - This is a common outcome when aldehydes react with azo/diazo compounds
D. Reduction to alcohols - Azo compounds are not typically reducing agents for aldehydes

Based on my chemistry knowledge, polymerization is the most characteristic effect when aldehydes react with azo or diazo compounds.
